claims.statement: The IC-Suite consists of five independently versioned toolchains: callidescope, codependix, codometer, coinagerie, and conformetry, each named for the command a user runs.
All IC-Suite toolchains share a five-layer architectural spine: core → configuration → analysis → output → cli, with each layer depending only downward.
The core layer holds only domain vocabulary (result/finding types, error classes, enums, unions, analyzer/validator contracts) and never holds services, modules, or anything executable.
The configuration layer holds the config file schema, loading, defaults, override resolution, and CLI flag resolution, producing one resolved configuration object; it never holds domain result types.
The analysis layer holds what the tool actually does (per-suite names and shapes) and never holds rendering or command wiring.
The output layer holds every render target (JSON, markdown, mermaid, anchor blocks, destination routing, delivery) and never holds analysis.
The cli layer holds only *.command.ts modules and nothing else, never any logic.

The nx plugin layer (callidescope, codependix, coinagerie and conformetry each have one) sits above cli and carries the layer:cli tag, not a sixth layer tag, because it is a second host for the same underlying toolchain.
The core-versus-configuration test: if a type describes what the tool produced, it belongs in core; if it describes what the user wrote in <tool>.config.ts, it belongs in configuration.
The analysis layer deliberately does not converge on a shared name across toolchains; it is governed by the rule: one package per independently usable analyzer, named for what it analyzes.
The *-agents and *-examples packages carry no layer tag and are not in the runtime chain; they are non-publishable (private: true, and excluded from nx.json release.projects).

Each suite's analysis layer packages are named per-suite: callidescope-graph; codependix-boundaries, file-imports, nestjs-modules, nx-projects; codometer-languages, measurement; coinagerie-languages, vocabulary; conformetry-generation, languages, validation.

The 29 publishable packages across the four suites version independently using Nx Release with projectsRelationship: "independent", conventional commits determine semver bumps, and Nx Release cascades patch bumps to internal dependents (updateDependents: "auto").
Releases operate at two tiers: repository root release (semantic-release, fixed version, no npm publishes) and publishable packages release (nx release, independent versioning, per-package tags).

Non-publishable packages are held back from npm by two repository gates: private: true in the manifest and the release.projects filter in nx.json, which excludes each *-agents and *-examples project; registry permissions are a third backstop.

No cross-toolchain @ic-suite/* shared package is created; the common ConfigurationService shape is a convention, not an imported type — each toolchain's core declares its own structurally identical shape.

codependix-nx-projects is an analysis-layer graph builder that reads the Nx project graph, not an Nx plugin; it keeps its name despite colliding with the nx plugin layer namespace, documented as a deliberate exception, and @codependix/nx is the plugin.

callidescope measures call-stack depth (longest chain of nested calls) and breadth (fan-out: number of direct callees per callable) for every traced entry point in a project and its Nx dependencies; the workspace default limits are maximumDepth 17 and maximumBreadth 2.

The callidescope CLI accepts --check with a set drawn from a fixed list of check names, --write to write reports, and --format to control stdout output; per-project config declares explicit maximumDepth and maximumBreadth limits.

The callidescope Nx plugin infers callidescope-trace, callidescope-depth, callidescope-breadth, and callidescope-restrict; the restrict target is the per-project gate and the one guard-code depends on.

codependix measures three graph levels (file imports, NestJS modules, Nx projects) and validates forbid/allow boundary rules plus cycle detection; rules are defined in configuration/ic-suite/codependix.config.ts with generic layer:* rules and per-package name:* rules.
The codependix map command accepts --check with boundaries and reports, --write to regenerate configured exports, --format for output, plus --json-output and --markdown-output paths.

The codependix Nx plugin infers the codependix-bound gate target (named by gateTargetName in nx.json); graphs are built over the project and its dependencies, and only violations charged to the project itself fail its gate.

codometer measures file sizes (lines, bytes), symbol counts, and comment-block word counts per language, with custom counters for project conventions such as Module Files, Service Files and Command Files.

The codometer measure command accepts --check, --output-json, --output-markdown and --inputs; the shared configuration defines zero-breach limits on every comment budget, plus directory tree breadth (12) and depth (9) limits.

The codometer Nx target runs through the integration:codometer batch executor with a check configuration that gates the project's limit and a write configuration that writes documentation/codometer.md; it depends on build, and build-projects depends on build and codometer so size limits gate builds.

conformetry validates generated code against templates using language-aware comparison; the workspace config at configuration/ic-suite/conformetry.config.ts defines generator groups with templates, input schemas, and instance globs.
The conformetry validate command accepts --config, --templates, --instances, --languages and --threshold (a minimum similarity ratio); a separate generate command scaffolds new files.
The conformetry Nx plugin infers the conformetry-validate target (named by validateTargetName in nx.json), configured from configuration/ic-suite/conformetry.config.ts.

The guard-code aggregator in nx.json depends on callidescope-restrict, catalog-manifests, codependix-bound, coinagerie-check, conformetry-validate, lockfile, project-ports, readme-projects and vscode-extensions; the build-projects aggregator depends on build and codometer so size limits gate packaging.

CI runs each toolchain gate as its own leg of the continuous-integration matrix: Guard (catalog-manifests, coinagerie-check, lockfile, project-ports, readme-projects, vscode-extensions), Callidescope Restrict, Codependix Bound, Conformetry Validate, and Build (build-projects, which includes codometer).

Coinagerie is the fifth IC-Suite toolchain: it lists the words a codebase uses and keeps markdown glossaries in step with the code via --check and --write, and its @coinagerie/nx plugin infers the per-project coinagerie-check gate.
The 36 publishable IC-Suite packages version independently with Nx release (projectsRelationship independent), and the 10 *-agents and *-examples projects are excluded by release.projects.
